chain.label: Low-visibility CAT II conditions at ORD
chain.trigger: visibility 1/2 statute mile in freezing fog, ceiling overcast at 100 feet agl...RVR on runway 14R of 1,400 feet variable to 1,800 feet

chain.label: Autopilot desensitization schedule not modified for higher approach speeds
chain.trigger: The autopilot installed on the airplane had not been modified in accordance with changes specified in two Sperry Service Bulletins...which recommended a change to the sensitivity schedule of the autopilot while in approach mode to accommodate new, higher approach airspeeds

chain.label: Autopilot commanded divergent oscillatory pitch changes near decision height
chain.trigger: the autopilot's 150-second desensitization rate was too slow for the accident airplane's approach speed, resulting in divergent pitch deviations at a low altitude at a critical time during the approach

caused_by.evidence: Calculations based on FDR data indicated that the accident airplane actually traveled this distance in about 100 seconds. As a result, during the approach, the autopilot sensitivity was consistently higher than its intended design value.

chain.label: Captain's sunglasses delayed visual acquisition of the runway environment
chain.trigger: he wore his sunglasses throughout the descent and approach until touchdown

caused_by.evidence: left his sunglasses on during the approach and landing, increasing the potential for visual illusions as a result of reduced visibility

chain.label: Crew failed to react in time to excessive pitch and descent-rate deviations
chain.trigger: the flight crew did not react in a proper and timely manner to excessive pitch deviations and descent rates by either initiating a go-around or adjusting the pitch attitude and thrust

caused_by.evidence: the airplane continued to pitch down to about -6° and descended well below the glideslope...the flight engineer stated, "ooh nose uh," and the captain did not disengage the autopilot or take any action to adjust the pitch attitude
a lack of horizon cues and what he described as a "low runway light intensity setting" delayed his visual acquisition of the runway environment

chain.label: Late corrective pitch-up and power addition insufficient to arrest descent
chain.trigger: The captain immediately pitched the airplane up to about 6° and added a substantial amount of power. These actions were not sufficient or timely enough to arrest the descent

caused_by.evidence: These actions were not sufficient or timely enough to arrest the descent

chain.label: Airplane impacted the ground short of the runway threshold
chain.trigger: the airplane continued to descend until it impacted the ground 314 feet short of the runway threshold, resulting in the separation of the main landing gear

caused_by.evidence: the airplane continued to descend until it impacted the ground 314 feet short of the runway threshold

chain.label: Airplane bounced, landed hard, and slid off the runway into mud
chain.trigger: The airplane then became airborne, touched down again on the runway, and then slid about 2,350 feet down the runway until coming to rest in an upright position in the mud about 250 feet to the right (west) of the runway

caused_by.evidence: the airplane touched down 160 feet short of the runway pavement...became airborne, touched down again on the runway, and then slid about 2,350 feet down the runway

chain.label: Minor injuries to 22 passengers and 1 flight attendant; aircraft substantially damaged
chain.trigger: Twenty-two passengers and one flight attendant received minor injuries, and the airplane was substantially damaged

caused_by.evidence: resulting in the separation of the main landing gear
Twenty-two passengers and one flight attendant reported that they received minor injuries during the accident...and subsequent emergency evacuation
